brief: Institutional positioning across the AI complex (Mag 7 and SOXX) turned increasingly bullish ahead of Monday's sell-off, but the call-put ratio's improvement has stalled in recent sessions, signaling institutions are pausing. Retail option activity in cyber stocks has picked up sharply from a low base, led by CrowdStrike (CRWD), which accounts for 53% of retail call activity in the basket and whose 1-month call buying sits in the 97th percentile of its own history. CRWD is the only major cyber name where retail is also buying the underlying stock alongside calls. Retail has not abandoned semis: SOXX-basket retail cash buying swung by more than $2bn over the past month, with NVDA accounting for 63% of inflows and, over the past two weeks, all net retail single-stock buying, meaning retail would have been a net seller of single names without NVDA. Still, 19 of 30 SOXX names saw positive retail buying over the month, led by Intel and Broadcom. Overall, positioning keeps clearing as systematic investors cut exposure and institutional buying slows, leaving a selective rather than indiscriminate risk-on tape. A broader index-level rally needs the Fed and geopolitical overhang to fade.
